q1: SELECT bar FROM Serves GROUP BY bar HAVING COUNT(beer) >= 5
q2: SELECT COUNT(beer) FROM serves GROUP BY bar
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT bar FROM Serves GROUP BY bar HAVING COUNT(beer) >= 5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(beer) FROM serves GROUP BY bar
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 returns the 'bar' names where the count of beers served is at least 5. Q2 returns the count of beers for each bar. The two queries produce different types of output (one returns bar names, the other returns counts) and have different conditions (Q1 has a HAVING filter, Q2 does not).
counterexample_dsp: A bar serving fewer than 5 beers will not appear in Q1 but will appear in Q2 with its beer count. For example, a bar serving only 3 beers will have a row in Q2 with COUNT(beer) = 3 but will not appear in Q1.
